newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Sky TV ponders NZ$800 mln float - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Sky TV ponders NZ$800 mln float - newspaper.

text.p: The owners of New Zealand's Sky TV have been courting sharebrokers with a view to an NZ$800 million share float, the New Zealand Herald newspaper reported on Friday.
A decision on whether the float of the pay television company would proceed is expected in about a month, with the share issue timed for the end of the year, the paper said.
A public issue is believed to be a fallback option after a deal with Independent Newspapers Ltd went sour earlier this year.
No reason was given for the breakdown in talks, which began in October and would have seen INL pay around NZ$650 million for an 83.2 percent slice of Sky.

The balance of the shareholding is held by state-oowned Television New Zealand, which was not part of the talks but was an apparent willing partner alongside INL, which is about half-owned by News Corp.
TVNZ does have a right of first refusal over share transfers and it has been given Commerce Commission approval to go higher. It is believed not to be in favour of a float, the paper said.
However, TVNZ's chief executive Chris Anderson would not comment.

The 83.2 percent holding in Sky is held between four groups -- the United States based HKP Partners (51.1 percent), Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corp (8.8 percent) and Tappenden Group (7.5 percent).
One analyst said that the move towards a float of Sky would force the hand of INL.
Despite talks breaking down, INL had never closed the door on the deal.
Set up in May 1990 by Craig Heatley and Terry Jarvis, Sky now has nearly 300,000 subscribers.
In April, Sky launched phase one of an analogue "direct to home" service carrying only the sports channel, to run in tandem with the existing "line of sight" UHF service.
Phase two in early 1998, or sooner, plans to introduce digital broadcasting, offering at least 20 channels, and eventually more than 40.
Sky, which is set to file its 1996 year accounts shortly, booked a loss of $9.8 million in the previous calendar year. It has accumulated a $128 million deficit since it began operating.
Its total balance sheet debt stands at around $147 million.
